Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.
Velocity is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude (speed) and direction.
When a car accelerates, its velocity changes, which means either its speed changes or its direction changes, or both.
Constant speed means the velocity is constant, so acceleration is zero.
Therefore, acceleration describes the change in velocity over time.
